title: Design a 50K RPS Distributed LLM Eval, Guardrails & Red Teaming Platform

spark.summary: Architect a 50,000 RPS LLM safety and evaluation platform with <25ms p99 inline guardrail sidecars, Kafka shadow-eval streams, a Ray/vLLM Judge Worker fleet scoring 1M+ daily traces, ClickHouse analytics, and automated CI/CD regression gates.
spark.keyTakeaway: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, guardrails & Red, split traffic at the API Gateway into a colocation-optimized <25ms inline guardrail sidecar and an asynchronous Kafka-to-Ray/vLLM judge pipeline backed by ClickHouse.
spark.byteSummary:
At 50,000 requests per second, running even a 300ms guardrail or judge synchronously would require thousands of extra GPUs and destroy user-facing TTFT. A production platform separates enforcement from deep auditing at the API Gateway.

On the synchronous path, every request passes through an Envoy/Rust API Gateway to a colocated Triton/TensorRT-LLM Inline Guardrail Sidecar (<25ms p99 budget) executing deterministic Aho-Corasick PII redaction and INT8 DeBERTa/Llama-Guard classification in parallel. Simultaneously, the gateway mirrors sampled traces (100% of blocked/high-risk, 5% of benign = ~1M–5M traces/day) into a partitioned Kafka shadow-eval topic.

A distributed Ray/vLLM Judge Worker fleet consumes from Kafka in micro-batches using continuous batching and prefix caching, scoring faithfulness, toxicity, and red-team resilience. Calibrated metrics land in ClickHouse for real-time drift alerting and power automated CI/CD deployment gates.

learningJourney.title: Traffic Sizing, SLA Budgets & Dual-Path Gateway Split
learningJourney.purpose: Size the 50K RPS inline fleet and 1M+ daily trace async judge fleet with clear latency/throughput targets.

explanation.foundation: At 50,000 RPS (~2 KB avg prompt+response = ~100 MB/s), the synchronous guardrail sidecar has a strict <25ms p99 budget (<=3ms gateway+network, <=12ms parallel input mesh, <=10ms streaming output window).
explanation.core: Using INT8 TensorRT-optimized DeBERTa-base (~1,200 req/s per L4/T4 GPU at batch=8, <=8ms p99), 50K RPS requires ~45–60 L4 GPUs with 30% headroom.
explanation.deepDive: Meanwhile, mirroring 2% of general traffic + 100% of flagged/canary traffic yields ~1M–2M daily traces for the async Ray/vLLM Judge fleet, which optimizes for throughput (tokens/sec) rather than TTFT.

learningJourney.title: Low-Latency Inline Guardrail Sidecar Architecture
learningJourney.purpose: Colocate Rust/Envoy proxy logic with Triton INT8 inference to stay under 25ms p99 at 50K RPS.

explanation.foundation: Cross-AZ network hops between an API Gateway and a remote guardrail microservice add 2–5ms per round trip—and twice that on streaming output checks.
explanation.core: Deploying the guardrail engine as a pod-local sidecar (or DaemonSet) using Unix Domain Sockets / shared memory between Envoy WASM/ext_proc and a Triton Inference Server (ONNX/TensorRT INT8) eliminates network serialization overhead.
explanation.deepDive: Dynamic micro-batching (max_queue_delay=2ms) groups concurrent requests on the same GPU without violating the 25ms p99 SLA.

sectionDiagram.title: Pod-Local Envoy ext_proc + Triton INT8 Guardrail Sidecar

cards.label: 2ms Batch Window
cards.detail: Capping Triton queue delay at 2ms boosts GPU throughput 4x while keeping p99 under 12ms.

cards.label: Tenant Policy Config
cards.detail: Compile per-tenant rule thresholds in an atomic in-memory map pushed via xDS/etcd.

sectionDiagram.summary: Colocating Envoy ext_proc with Rust Aho-Corasick and Triton INT8 dynamic batching meets the 25ms p99 budget at 50K RPS.
sectionDiagram.caption: UDS/shared-memory sidecar colocation removes cross-AZ RPC latency from every token window.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a 50K RPS Distributed LLM Eval, Guardrails & Red Teaming Platform without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, guardrails & Red, split traffic at the API Gateway into a colocation-optimized <25ms inline guardrail sidecar and an asynchronous Kafka-to-Ray/vLLM judge pipeline backed by ClickHouse.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a 50K RPS Distributed LLM Eval, Guardrails & Red Teaming Platform experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Kafka Shadow-Eval Pipeline, PII Scrubbing & Priority Queues
learningJourney.purpose: Ingest 1M+ daily production traces reliably with tenant isolation, PII scrubbing, and priority tiers.

explanation.foundation: Shadow-eval streams cannot store raw customer SSNs or secrets in long-lived evaluation lakes.
explanation.core: Before writing to Kafka (`eval.traces.v1`), the gateway's async mirror applies irreversible token-preserving PII redaction (`<EMAIL_1>`, `<CARD_1>`). Topics are partitioned by `tenant_id` hash with separate priority topics: `eval.high_priority` (blocked requests, user thumbs-down, canary deployments) and `eval.sample` (2% random baseline).
explanation.deepDive: Backpressure policies ensure consumer lag in `eval.sample` never starves `eval.high_priority` or CI/CD release gates.

sectionDiagram.title: PII-Scrubbed Kafka Shadow-Eval & Priority Partitioning

cards.label: Consistent Tagging
cards.detail: Token-preserving placeholders (<PERSON_1>) let judges still score grammar and faithfulness.

cards.label: Canary Boost
cards.detail: Automatically bump sampling from 2% to 25% for newly deployed model/prompt versions.

sectionDiagram.summary: Irreversible edge PII scrubbing and dual-priority Kafka topics protect customer privacy while guaranteeing fast feedback on incidents and canaries.
sectionDiagram.caption: Priority partitioning prevents baseline trace volume from delaying canary regression alerts.

learningJourney.title: Distributed Ray / vLLM Judge Worker Fleet
learningJourney.purpose: Maximize tokens/sec on 1M+ daily evals using Ray Data micro-batching, vLLM prefix caching, and structured outputs.

explanation.foundation: Evaluating 1M traces/day across 3 rubric dimensions (faithfulness, toxicity, jailbreak resistance) requires ~3M judge calls/day (~35–100 calls/sec sustained, 3x peak).
explanation.core: Ray actors pull 256-trace micro-batches from Kafka and dispatch them to vLLM workers configured with Automatic Prefix Caching (APC) so the 800-token judge rubric is cached once across all 256 requests.

sectionDiagram.title: Ray + vLLM Continuous-Batched Judge Workers

cards.label: Spot GPU Savings
cards.detail: Because async judges tolerate 10-30s restarts, running on spot GPUs cuts eval cost by ~60%.

cards.label: Length Bucketing
cards.detail: Sorting micro-batches by prompt length minimizes padding waste in continuous batching.

sectionDiagram.summary: Ray Data micro-batching paired with vLLM prefix caching and FSM-guided JSON decoding maximizes judge throughput on spot GPUs.
sectionDiagram.caption: Prefix-caching the judge rubric across 256-trace batches eliminates redundant prefill compute.

learningJourney.title: ClickHouse Analytical Store & Real-Time Drift Alerting
learningJourney.purpose: Store millions of daily eval scores and audit logs for sub-second slicing by model, prompt version, and tenant.

explanation.foundation: Transactional Postgres tables choke on analytical aggregations over 30M+ monthly eval rows (`GROUP BY prompt_version, model_id, violation_type`).
explanation.core: ClickHouse (`MergeTree` partitioned by `toYYYYMM(ts)`, ordered by `(tenant_id, model_version, ts)`) ingests judge verdicts via Kafka Connect / Vector at >100K rows/sec with ZSTD compression.
explanation.deepDive: Materialized views pre-aggregate 5-minute rolling windows for faithfulness, ASR, and block rate, firing PagerDuty/Slack alerts within 2 minutes if a canary's violation rate exceeds the baseline + 1.5% threshold.

sectionDiagram.title: ClickHouse MergeTree Metrics & Rolling-Window Drift Alerts

cards.label: Immutable Audit Trail
cards.detail: Retain hashed prompt/verdict metadata in S3/Iceberg for 1-7 years for compliance audits.

cards.label: Dimension Cardinality
cards.detail: Keep high-cardinality trace_id out of the primary sort prefix to preserve scan speed.

sectionDiagram.summary: ClickHouse MergeTree tables and 5-minute materialized views power sub-second slice-and-dice analytics and rapid canary rollback.
sectionDiagram.caption: Materialized rollups detect safety or faithfulness drift within minutes of a canary rollout.

learningJourney.title: Distributed Red-Teaming Sandbox & Scheduled Attack Campaigns
learningJourney.purpose: Execute multi-turn adversarial campaigns in isolated sandboxes without risking production data or rate limits.

explanation.foundation: Running 50,000 adversarial red-team probes against production endpoints pollutes customer analytics and risks triggering real MCP tool side effects.
explanation.core: Instead, a dedicated Ray Red-Team Orchestrator spins up ephemeral, network-isolated target sandboxes with mocked tool backends (e.g., fake SQL/email/CRM stubs that record attempted exfiltration).
explanation.deepDive: Campaigns run both on-demand for major model releases and nightly against production shadow configs, logging every successful jailbreak directly into the ClickHouse vulnerability registry and GitHub regression queue.

sectionDiagram.title: Isolated Ephemeral Red-Team Sandboxes & Tool Mocks

cards.label: Canary Trap Tokens
cards.detail: Seed mocked tool responses with canary strings to detect indirect prompt-injection exfiltration.

cards.label: Budget Caps
cards.detail: Enforce per-campaign token budgets so multi-turn attacker loops cannot runaway-spend.

sectionDiagram.summary: Sandboxed red-team campaigns probe mocked agent tools with canary tokens to catch exfiltration and multi-turn jailbreaks safely.
sectionDiagram.caption: Mocked tool sandboxes with canary strings verify indirect prompt-injection resistance without prod risk.

learningJourney.title: Automated CI/CD Deployment Gates & Progressive Rollback
learningJourney.purpose: Wire ClickHouse eval baselines and Ray test suites into GitOps deployment pipelines.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Automated CI/CD Deployment Gates & Progressive Rollback** as the intuition layer for Design a 50K RPS Distributed LLM Eval, Guardrails & Red Teaming Platform: Wire ClickHouse eval baselines and Ray test suites into GitOps deployment pipelines.
explanation.core: When an engineer opens a PR updating a system prompt, guardrail threshold, or model weights, GitHub Actions / ArgoCD triggers a tiered eval job: Tier 1 (200 critical smoke + top-50 red-team probes, <2 min) blocks PR merge; Tier 2 (3,000 stratified cases with paired bootstrap 95% CIs) gates staging-to-production promotion. Once promoted to 5% canary traffic, Argo Rollouts polls ClickHouse's 5-minute materialized views and automatically aborts and rolls back if inline block rate jumps >2% or async faithfulness drops >1.5%.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, automated ci/cd deployment gates & progressive rollback becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production 50K RPS LLM evaluation and safety architecture combining UDS/Triton INT8 sidecars, non-blocking priority Kafka mirroring, APC-enabled Ray/vLLM spot judges, ClickHouse rollups, and canary-trap red-team sandboxes.

knowledgeChecks.question: At 50,000 RPS, why should the API Gateway mirror shadow-eval traces to Kafka using a non-blocking bounded ring buffer rather than a synchronous Kafka producer?

options.text: Kafka does not support JSON or Protobuf messages.
options.feedback: Kafka natively supports any binary format including Protobuf and JSON.

options.text: A synchronous Kafka call would couple live user TTFT to Kafka broker latency and cause cascading 50K RPS outages if Kafka slows down.
options.feedback: Correct! Shadow evaluation is non-critical-path; dropping a few mirrored traces on Kafka backpressure protects live user traffic.

options.text: Non-blocking buffers automatically compute Cohen's kappa.
options.feedback: Cohen's kappa is computed offline during judge calibration.

options.text: Synchronous Kafka calls bypass the Triton INT8 guardrail sidecar.
options.feedback: Guardrail sidecars run on the request path regardless of how telemetry is emitted.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Decoupling telemetry with a non-blocking bounded buffer ensures async evaluation issues never degrade live 50K RPS availability.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does Automatic Prefix Caching (APC) in the Ray/vLLM Judge Worker fleet significantly reduce GPU cost when scoring 1M daily traces?

options.text: It compresses ClickHouse MergeTree partitions using ZSTD.
options.feedback: ZSTD compression is a storage feature in ClickHouse, not vLLM GPU caching.

options.text: It caches the KV-blocks of the shared 800-token judge rubric across micro-batches so only the unique trace payload needs prefill.
options.feedback: Correct! Caching the shared rubric KV blocks eliminates ~40-60% of redundant prefill compute across 1M daily judge calls.

options.text: It replaces the LLM judge with Aho-Corasick regex matching.
options.feedback: APC optimizes LLM transformer prefill; it does not replace the model with regex.

options.text: It routes user traffic directly to spot GPUs.
options.feedback: Spot GPUs are used for async judge workers, not live user traffic.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: APC deduplicates the shared rubric prompt across thousands of trace evaluations in GPU HBM.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must an automated red-teaming campaign run against a sandboxed agent with mocked tools and canary tokens rather than production endpoints?

options.text: Mocked tools prevent prompt-injected exploits from mutating real databases while canary tokens prove whether data exfiltration occurred.
options.feedback: Correct! Sandboxed mocks protect production state and provide deterministic signals (canary leaks) of indirect prompt-injection success.

options.text: Production endpoints cannot run Envoy ext_proc.
options.feedback: Production endpoints do run Envoy ext_proc; sandboxing is for safety and isolation.

options.text: Canary tokens speed up Triton INT8 dynamic batching.
options.feedback: Canary tokens are security tripwires, not inference batching optimizations.

options.text: Sandboxed agents do not require any LLM weights.
options.feedback: The sandboxed agent still runs the target LLM weights; only external side-effecting tools are mocked.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Tool mocking + canary tokens safely test end-to-end agentic exploit paths without risking real-world side effects.

beginner.summary: A large-scale AI safety platform uses fast sidecar filters at the gateway to block bad prompts in under 25ms, while sending copies of traffic to background AI judges and analytics dashboards.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, Guardrails & Red, split traffic at the API Gateway into a colocation-optimized <25ms inline guardrail sidecar and an asynchronous Kafka-to-Ray/vLLM judge pipeline backed by ClickHouse.
beginner.byteSummary:
Handling 50,000 AI requests per second means you cannot run slow safety checks on every single message in real time. Instead, a fast sidecar next to the gateway strips private data and blocks obvious attacks in under 25 milliseconds.

At the same time, a copy of sampled traffic is scrubbed of private info and sent through Kafka to background judge servers. Those servers score accuracy and safety, save the results in ClickHouse, and automatically pause software updates if a new version scores worse.

intermediate.summary: A 50K RPS LLM governance platform pairs pod-local Envoy/Triton INT8 guardrail sidecars (<25ms p99) with PII-scrubbed Kafka streams, Ray/vLLM judge fleets, ClickHouse rollups, and Argo CI/CD gates.

intermediate.byteSummary:
The API Gateway enforces <25ms p99 safety via pod-local Envoy ext_proc + Rust Aho-Corasick + Triton INT8 DeBERTa sidecars, while non-blocking buffers mirror PII-scrubbed traces into priority Kafka topics.

Spot-GPU Ray/vLLM workers use Automatic Prefix Caching and guided JSON decoding to score 1M+ daily traces into ClickHouse MergeTree tables. Materialized 5-minute views power Argo Rollouts canary aborts alongside tiered pre-merge CI suites.

advanced.summary: Production 50K RPS LLM evaluation and safety architecture combining UDS/Triton INT8 sidecars, non-blocking priority Kafka mirroring, APC-enabled Ray/vLLM spot judges, ClickHouse rollups, and canary-trap red-team sandboxes.

Colocating Envoy ext_proc with Rust Aho-Corasick and 2ms-batched Triton INT8 classifiers over UDS meets <25ms p99 at 50K RPS (~55 L4 GPUs). Non-blocking gateway mirroring scrubs PII and splits `eval.high_priority` from `eval.sample`.

Sandboxed red-teamers test mocked tools with canary tokens, while Argo Rollouts polls 5-minute rollups for automated rollback.
